India’s first Asian Games MMA medallist came within 700 grams of a place in the final at Aichi-Nagoya. From an eight-time national judo champion to a ju-jitsu world champion, Tariyal’s journey has been shaped by financial strain, doubts over her age and her husband Kapil Hooda’s unwavering faith.

title: Ludhiana teen wins Eco-Hero award for pollinator gardens
description: Gunisha Kaur, a 16-year-old from Ludhiana, creates pollinator gardens to support biodiversity and inclusion. Her initiative, Buzzing Blooms, transforms urban spaces into chemical-free habitats for both pollinators and children. Over 24 months, the project recorded significant increases in pollinator species and bee visitation. Engaging local communities, Buzzing Blooms focuses on inclusive outdoor spaces catering to diverse needs. Through workshops and advocacy, Kaur aims to foster environmental action among youth.

title: 'I can always talk to you like this': On cam, IAS officer abuses woman during meeting
description: Kumar Rajeev Ranjan, an IAS officer, reportedly insulted a subordinate female officer during a video meeting. This incident has sparked widespread condemnation from various political parties in Jammu and Kashmir. Ranjan allegedly used derogatory language and threatened to get the officer suspended. While the labour department claimed the video is fabricated, JKAS officers assert its authenticity. Numerous calls for inquiry and action against Ranjan have been made following this incident.

title: Bigg Boss 20: Qazi recalls saying no to Ekta Kapoor rockstar show; slams media scrutiny

However, he declined a prominent role from Ekta Kapoor, which sparked misunderstandings. Under pressure while discussing the opportunity, he soon faced backlash from the media, who branded him arrogant for his choice, despite having already committed to a film project.

title: Para-shuttlers challenge Para Asian Games non-selection in Delhi HC
description: Chirag Baretha, a decorated para-badminton player, and fellow para-shuttlers have filed a petition after being excluded from India’s 2026 Asian Para Games contingent despite meeting the selection criteria. Alleging unfair treatment and procedural irregularities, they have challenged the roles of the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and the Badminton Association of India (BAI), raising questions about transparency in the selection process.

title: Oil prices dip marginally as US weighs easing sanctions on ‘shadow fleet’ tankers
description: Amid fluctuating oil markets, current tensions in the Middle East and possible shifts in US sanctions have resulted in a marginal decline in oil prices. WTI crude is priced at $97.31, with Brent crude at $105.40. While recent moves to lift restrictions on certain vessels aim to counter soaring global freight rates, the International Energy Agency's diesel release hasn't completely eased concerns about oil supply.

title: Zelenskyy’s worst nightmare is here: Ukraine runs out of Patriot missiles
description: Ukraine's shortage of Patriot air defence missiles has left it exposed to Russian missile attacks and critical infrastructure damage. Recent attacks have targeted power plants in Kyiv and Kharkiv, resulting in casualties. Relations between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the US government have soured amid disputes over energy and military support. Additionally, limitations on Starlink connectivity have disrupted military operations in Ukraine.

title: 'Reel ke chakkar mein thuk jaoge': Sooryavanshi warns paps - Watch
description: Teenage cricket star Vaibhav Sooryavanshi went viral after jokingly warning airport paparazzi, “Reel ke chakkar mein thuk jaoge,” urging them to prioritise safety over filming. He was in New Delhi to meet PM Narendra Modi during a felicitation ceremony for India’s Asian Games contingent. Modi encouraged athletes to inspire children, highlighting sports’ role in teaching discipline, resilience and perseverance through his message, “Jo Khelega, Woh Khilega.”

title: Imran Khan was just passing through, didn’t take part in Mumbai protests: Lawyers
description: Imran Khan has been asked by the FRRO to leave India by October 28, raising legal concerns. Lawyers argue that he did not participate in the protest and only passed through the area. The police have charged the protestors for illegal assembly due to lacking permission for the demonstration. Legal representatives plan to seek CCTV footage to support Khan's claims regarding his involvement.

title: Absconding in UP bizman murder case, accused model Shraddha Dubey may be in Nepal
description: The investigation into Shiva Sharma's death has led authorities to search for Shraddha Dubey across borders. CCTV footage reportedly shows Shraddha, her sister Rashmi, and an associate Adil in Nepal. They are believed to have fled Lucknow soon after the incident, raising suspicion. Sharma's family has alleged foul play, while Dubey maintains her innocence and claims he died by suicide.

title: Maya Angelou: When people show you who they are, believe them the first time
description: Maya Angelou's wisdom teaches us to pay attention to actions that unveil true character within relationships. Oprah Winfrey underscores the need to view consistent behavior as significant rather than waving them off as simple mistakes. A relationship thrives on accountability, fostering awareness of recurring patterns. Although trust and forgiveness are vital components, they should never excuse ongoing disrespect or lack of integrity.

title: ‘Lacks common sense’: Ashwin blasts India over Kuldeep’s exclusion
description: Former India spinner R Ashwin criticised the team management for dropping Kuldeep Yadav from the last two T20Is against the West Indies, saying the decision “lacks a bit of common sense.” Ashwin argued Kuldeep’s variations troubled the visiting batters and could have saved India 15–20 runs. However, he supported Kuldeep’s exclusion in Indore due to the ground’s small dimensions.

title: 56-year-old chestnut grove, one of America’s last, at risk from AI data center
description: In West Virginia, plans for a new data center, the Monarch Compute Campus, could mean the removal of around 200 blight-resistant American chestnut trees. Planted in the 1970s, these trees are vital for future restoration projects. Conservationists express concern over the potential loss of this endangered genetic resource, making its fate precarious amidst development considerations and the push for sustainability.

title: 'Hanuman Ansh' box office: India collection stands at Rs 338.98 cr

The film's overseas gross has reached Rs 48.30 crore, contributing to a global total of Rs 448.33 crore. However, Thursday's net earnings declined significantly compared to the previous day. The Hindi and Telugu versions of the movie recorded varying occupancy rates across different shows.

The enforcement drive has resulted in more than 300 fixed penalty notices worth around £134,000. England recorded over 1.26 million fly-tipping incidents last year, a 9% increase, with serious offenders facing prison sentences.

CCTV footage revealed a 10-year-old girl throwing the toddler down the stairwell from the sixth floor. The toddler was playing outside when her mother sent a brother to find her, leading to the grim discovery. Residents rushed the injured child to a doctor, but she was pronounced dead shortly after.

title: Uttarakhand minister files FIR against husband, alleges assault, plot to kill her
description: Uttarakhand cabinet minister Rekha Arya has taken the courageous step of filing a police report against her husband Girdhari Lal Sahu. In her allegations, she has accused him of a range of serious offenses, including physical assault, threats towards their children, infidelity, and even a conspiracy to kill her. Arya alleges that Sahu misled her about his marital status and resorted to violence when confronted about his extramarital affairs.

title: "I only drink on weekends": Can occasional drinking still damage the liver even without any symptoms?
description: Regular weekend drinking might feel harmless, but it can severely compromise your liver health. The liver, tasked with processing alcohol, may incur cellular damage and cause inflammation over time. Persistent episodes of binge drinking can lead to conditions like fatty liver disease, which often shows no symptoms. Without attention, this damage could escalate to fibrosis or cirrhosis, impairing liver function and overall well-being.

title: US temple attack plot: Teen’s alleged manifesto describes Indians as ‘subhumans’
description: A 19-year-old white supremacist's intention to attack a temple near Chicago was disrupted by a rifle malfunction. Following the incident, concerned colleagues notified authorities after he expressed his intentions via messages. Police arrested Alexandros Paporakis, uncovering alarming materials including a manifesto that targeted several communities. The case has raised serious safety concerns among Hindu organizations about worship places.

title: Meet Gabriella Rothberg, 17, co-inventor of patented genetically engineered tomato
description: A sandwich idea at 15 led Miami student Gabriella Rothberg to develop genetically engineered tomatoes designed to produce heme, an iron-containing molecule associated with meat flavour. Now 17, she is listed alongside her father on a US patent issued in June 2026. The project remains experimental, with taste and nutritional benefits yet to be established.

title: Ex-IAS Divya launches party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
description: Divya Mittal, an ex-IAS officer, has established the Jan Neeti Bharat party in preparation for the forthcoming elections. With a focus on enhancing citizen participation in policymaking rather than adhering to conventional governance methods, she aims to make a significant impact. Her decision to retire after 13 years in civil service aligns with a trend of bureaucrats entering politics.

title: Michael Dell loses $20 billion in one day after Barclays downgrade
description: Michael Dell experienced a substantial decline in net worth, dropping more than $20 billion in just one day. This decline was prompted by a major decrease in his company's stock value following an analyst downgrade. Earlier this year, Dell's net worth had notably increased, bringing him closer to the highest billionaires in the world.

title: No more guessing who's calling! Govt mandates caller ID display from Nov 1
description: The Department of Telecommunications is preparing to roll out Calling Name Presentation, a feature that shows the caller's name in addition to their number on the recipient's screen. This functionality will first be implemented on 4G networks before extending to other versions. Users will have the choice to opt-out if they utilize the calling line identification restriction service, striking a balance between enhancing caller recognition and safeguarding data privacy.
